grids.E_grid: G1 with theta=0 dropped (kappa(0)=1 identically, spec 1.4 degeneracy note) -> 800 nodes
grids.fine_E_grid: fine G1 with theta=0 dropped -> 16000 nodes

constraints.A_and_D: automatic and exact for real matched alpha (not imposed)

solver.name: scipy.optimize.minimize
solver.objective_gradient: analytic (trivial: grad = e_n, the delta unit vector)
solver.constraint_jacobian: finite-difference (SLSQP default 2-point); explicitly permitted by the brief

bounds.note: not specified in the brief; added purely as a numerical-stability guard after observing float64 cosh/sinh overflow (|alpha|~700+) stall SLSQP at n=5 without them. True optima found are all O(0.1-0.5), far inside these bounds -- see run's report for the ~25x n=5 slowdown this was meant to (and did not fully) fix.

starts.random_distribution: alpha_j ~ N(0, 0.35^2) i.i.d., matched via alpha_n := -sum(alpha_0..alpha_{n-1})
starts.antisym_distribution: free half of alpha_j ~ N(0, 0.35^2), filled in via alpha_j = -alpha_{n-j} (n odd, no fixed midpoint)
continuation: best alpha_first at (n, d-1, sigma), reused directly (same length n)
best alpha_first at (n-2, d, sigma), embedded into length n via a zero-contrast layer appended at each end of the (n-1)-length full alpha vector -- disclosed choice, not specified in the brief
starts.discard_rule: SLSQP res.success==False discarded outright; else re-checked on the FINE (16001-node) grid at tolerance 1e-9 (spec Sec 2/3) and discarded if infeasible there
starts.selection_and_reporting: best (min) delta_fine among fine-grid-feasible converged starts; delta_fine (not the solver's coarse-grid delta) is the reported value, per spec Sec 3

rng.note: sweep_seed = gates_seed + 100, a single np.random.default_rng stream consumed sequentially across all 66 cases in n,d,sigma order -- so results are only exactly reproducible by replaying that same case order with the same seed.
